name: Raúl Castro
role: Cuban revolutionary; Minister of the Armed Forces (1959–2008), President of Cuba (2008–2018), First Secretary of the Communist Party of Cuba (2011–2021)
summary: Cuban communist and revolutionary who led the island's armed forces for almost five decades before succeeding his brother Fidel. He kept one-party rule, state ownership of the main means of production, and the doctrine of defence of the revolution, while opening limited private work, land in usufruct, foreign investment, travel abroad and diplomatic relations with the United States. He proposed and applied two-term limits to himself and handed office to Díaz-Canel in 2018 and party leadership in 2021.

universal-healthcare.rationale: His 2021 central report calls the free, universal, accessible health system a result possible only under socialism and warns that privatization would dismantle it; as head of state he kept it free for all.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The programme he led keeps socialist planning as the main way of directing the economy, with the market only taken into account; in 2021 he rejected privatization and defended the state monopoly of foreign trade.

public-ownership.rationale: In 2016 he stated that ownership by the whole people of the fundamental means of production is and will remain the main form of the national economy; the constitution says the same.

unions-good.rationale: In 2016 he urged workers to unite to be stronger through the CTC and mocked Western labels calling it the 'single' union; he did not discuss unions' general social value beyond this.

property-fundamental.rationale: Under his leadership private property was recognised only in a 'complementary' role, with limits and no concentration of property or wealth; he stressed socialist state property as the base of workers' power.

regulate-corporations.rationale: In 2016 he said private enterprise must act within well-defined limits regulated by law and that the state must act against price speculation by intermediaries; in 2015 he backed Ecuador against transnationals doing ecological damage.

cut-welfare.rationale: Evidence points both ways: he called the ration book an egalitarian disincentive to work and cut subsidies and gratuities, but kept free health and education and insisted no one would be left unprotected.

worker-ownership.rationale: He promoted cooperatives and other non-state forms but kept the state enterprise as the main form of ownership, so the record does not show collective worker ownership as his aim.

socialized-markets.rationale: He accepted markets inside a planned socialist system with state enterprises as the core, but also allowed private micro-businesses and self-employment, so the 'only if owned by workers or the public' condition does not match his record.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: In 2016 he said supply and demand can coexist with planning, citing the reform in China and renewal in Vietnam, while the Communist Party stays in leadership; he did not use the phrase 'market economy'.

central-planning.rationale: He called the excessively centralized model an obstacle and moved to decentralize, yet kept planning as the principal way of directing the economy.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The programme he led sets an investment policy steered by the state plan and keeps the state sector in the areas that decide national development, with foreign capital only as a complement.

widespread-small-property.rationale: He kept state ownership as the main form and limited private property to a complementary role, though the programme also bars concentration of non-state property.

collective-farming.rationale: He drove Decree-Law 259 and its expansion, which hands idle state land in usufruct to individual farmers, and the programme promotes small farmers and usufructuaries alongside cooperatives.

taxation-theft.rationale: He required self-employed workers to meet their obligations 'including tax obligations' with the full rigor of the law, and the programme builds a tax system on generality and equity.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He repeatedly said no Cuban would be left unprotected and that shock therapy against the most needy would never be applied; in 2015 he said Cuba stood with the poor and sick.

job-guarantee.rationale: He launched the reduction of inflated state payrolls in the state sector and pushed workers toward self-employment rather than guaranteeing jobs.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: The programme he led encourages foreign investment, exports and integration (ALBA), and he sought foreign partners rather than a closed bloc.

national-resource-control.rationale: The constitution places land, mines, waters and natural resources in the property of the whole people, and in 2015 he backed Ecuador against transnational companies imposing abusive conditions.

free-trade.rationale: In 2015 he said the proposed Free Trade Area of the Americas would have destroyed the sovereignty and economy of the region, and in 2021 he defended the socialist state monopoly of foreign trade.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: At the UN in 2015 he demanded financial resources, technology transfer and special treatment for African and Caribbean countries, and urged multiplying aid to Haiti.

colonial-reparations.rationale: In 2015 he demanded reparations from colonial powers for slavery and colonialism for Caribbean nations, at the UN and in Panama, and repeated it in 2021.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: In 2015 he called for a transparent and equitable financial system, an end to Bretton Woods privileges and a more just international order centred on people.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He adopted Fidel's view that underdevelopment results from conquest, colonization and imperialist plunder, and said debts had been paid several times without falling; he did not describe a surplus-transfer mechanism.

delink-world-market.rationale: He pursued integration into world trade, foreign investment and ties with China, Vietnam, Russia and the EU rather than a break with rich countries.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: The programme he led seeks foreign capital, credit and cooperation and the lifting of the US embargo, while also stressing import substitution.

distribute-by-need.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

moral-incentives.rationale: The 2021 report says the model fails to give enough incentives for work, and the programme he led links worker income to results; he criticised egalitarianism and the ration book as a disincentive.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: He restated the socialist principle that distribution follows work, saying socialism means equal rights and opportunities, not egalitarianism, and the programme ties income to results; the constitution repeats the formula.

equal-outcomes.rationale: In his 2011 report he said socialism means equality of rights and opportunities, 'not egalitarianism', and called the ration book's egalitarianism harmful.

free-public-college.rationale: He repeatedly describes Cuba's education as free and universal, and in 2021 warned that privatization would dismantle the free national education system; the programme keeps university study free.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: In 2021 he warned that privatization would undo the free universal health and education systems, and the programme keeps them state-run.

local-essentials-public.rationale: The constitution places waters and other resources in public property, and in 2021 he defended state-run universal health care against privatization.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: The programme he led calls for raising national crude oil and gas output, new exploration in the Gulf of Mexico economic zone and more refining, alongside renewable energy.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Decree-Law 259, which he drove, hands idle state land to farmers in usufruct; land remains state property unless held by individuals or cooperatives.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: He limited private enterprise to a complementary role with no concentration of property or wealth and a regulatory framework set by law.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The programme he led bars concentration of property and wealth in the non-state sector; this is a limit on wealth, not a statement about liberty.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He ties independence to social justice and socialism, saying Cuba could avoid collapse only under the socialist system, but did not say so about independence in general.

self-interest-moral.rationale: In 2021 he described egoism, greed and the drive for higher income as motives behind calls for privatization, which he rejected.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: At the UN in 2015 he condemned the waste of natural and human resources in irrational and unsustainable consumerism, and in 2016 he criticised consumer-society values as eroding commitment.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: In 2016 he said state ownership of the main means of production is the base of the real power of the workers.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He moved toward subsidising people rather than products and limiting social assistance to those unable to work, but kept health and education free and universal.

ban-cartels.rationale: No recorded position found in the sources consulted.

separate-church-state.rationale: The 2019 constitution declares the republic secular and separates religious institutions from the State; in 2011 he noted Cuba's secular tradition and good relations with churches.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: In 2011 he spoke of unity between believers and non-believers and of improved relations with churches; the constitution guarantees religious liberty and treats religions equally.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: In 2011 he called for more blacks, mestizos, women and young people in decision-making posts, and in 2021 reported a government commission to address racial discrimination.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: In 2011 he asked for fair proportions of race and gender in the composition of cadres, which supports racial considerations in appointment.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: In 2021 he said the party keeps confronting prejudice and all discrimination, and the constitution bars discrimination by skin colour or ethnic origin.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: He backs confronting 'all types of discrimination' and the constitution prohibits discrimination by sex, skin colour, belief and other grounds.

women-suffrage.rationale: In 2011 he reported the share of women in the National Assembly and in cadres and said women hold the same political rights; the constitution guarantees all citizens the right to vote and stand.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: The constitution bars discrimination by sex and recognises the right to succession, with equal rights for all; he stated equal pay for equal work as a human right in 2016.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The constitution, drafted by a commission he chaired, bases marriage on the equality of rights and obligations of spouses.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He said equal pay for men and women for equal work is a human right in Cuba, and the constitution bars sex discrimination.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: His 2011 report commits the state to defend national identity and the conservation of cultural heritage.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He committed the state to conserve cultural heritage and national identity in 2011, the opposite of sacrificing it.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: In 2011 he said powerful media consortiums hide or distort facts to deceive public opinion, and in 2015 he objected to a handful of firms setting what the world reads and sees.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: In 2015 he said it is unacceptable that fewer than ten corporations decide what is read, seen or heard worldwide; he did not speak of press freedom in these terms.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: He repeatedly joined patriotic loyalty with social justice, speaking of fidelity to ideals of independence and social justice and of patriotic convictions sustaining socialism.

gradual-change.rationale: He described reforms as proceeding 'without haste but without pause', with order and discipline and no improvisation, within existing institutions.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He urged banishing immobility based on dogmas and slogans, but set irreversible limits in 2021 beyond which reform would be refused.

revolution-justified.rationale: He took part in the armed insurrection against Batista; in 2015 he defended the revolution and said harassment of revolutionary processes only brings more revolution; the constitution affirms the legitimacy of armed resistance and liberation struggles.

political-violence-never.rationale: He defends the armed rebellion that began at Moncada and told the Americas that actions of solidarity that 'may be considered terrorist' were chosen over surrender when Cuba was cornered.

one-party-rule.rationale: In 2016 he declared that Cuba has a single party 'and with much honour', and in 2021 that the single party will always be defended against calls for multiparty democracy; the constitution names the Communist Party as the superior driving force.

democracy-best.rationale: He rejected 'sacrosanct bourgeois democracy' and multiparty competition as a trap, while claiming Cuba's democracy should be perfected within one party.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He rejected free multiparty competition as 'bourgeois democracy' and kept a single-party system; the constitution declares the socialist system irrevocable.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He says the Party and Revolution have majority support, but no competitive elections or legal opposition operated under him.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He promoted public discussion of the Lineamientos and the draft constitution and called for greater citizen participation in fundamental decisions.

constituent-assembly.rationale: The 2019 constitution was drafted by a commission of Assembly deputies he chaired and approved by referendum, not by an elected constituent assembly.

separated-powers.rationale: The constitution keeps the National Assembly as the supreme organ of state power and the Party as the superior driving force, rather than separate checking bodies.

term-limits.rationale: In 2011 he proposed limiting political and state posts to two consecutive five-year terms, including himself; he left the presidency in 2018 and the constitution limits the president to two terms.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He proposed in 2011 that top political and state posts be limited to two five-year terms, applying to himself, and stepped down in 2018; the constitution bars a third presidential term.

recall-officials.rationale: The constitution says deputies' mandates are revocable at any moment, as the law provides.

recallable-delegates.rationale: The constitution makes representatives' mandates revocable at any time and requires them to report to their electors.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: As head of state and chair of the drafting commission he kept election of the President by the National Assembly rather than by popular vote.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He held the posts of head of state and Commander-in-Chief of the armed forces, and the constitution gives the President command of the forces and power to propose ministers.

party-commands-army.rationale: He said the strategy of Guerra de Todo el Pueblo works 'under the direction of the Party', but the constitution also makes the President commander-in-chief.

military-guardian-role.rationale: He described the armed forces as the uniformed people defending the socialist system and in 2021 reaffirmed their role in defending socialism, which the constitution also states.

conscription.rationale: In 2021 he called active military service the main route of military preparation and urged extending it; the constitution provides for obligatory military service.

people-in-arms.rationale: He kept a professional armed force and conscription, treating the 'war of all the people' as a doctrine run under the Party and armed forces.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Human Rights Watch reports that his government repressed dissent through arrests and denied legal recognition to groups such as the Ladies in White; he described outside funding of dissent as subversion.

party-controls-media.rationale: The constitution makes the fundamental media socialist property or that of party and mass organisations; Human Rights Watch reports blocking of independent sites.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: He condemned US financing of projects of subversion in Cuba, and Human Rights Watch reports the government treats unrecognized groups as illegal.

corporate-influence.rationale: At the UN in 2015 he said electoral systems and traditional parties that depend on money and advertising are distant from their peoples.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He made the Communist Party the guarantee of national unity and rejected splitting it, and the constitution makes it the superior force of society.

vanguard-party.rationale: In 2016 he defined the Party as guarantor of national unity; the constitution calls it the organised vanguard of the nation, Marxist-Leninist, led by Fidelista ideas.

independent-unions.rationale: He defended a single trade union centre, the CTC, and ridiculed Western press labelling it 'single'; no independent unions were recognised under him.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He served simultaneously as president and First Secretary of the Communist Party, openly partisan.

state-harmful.rationale: He built policy on a strong state: in 2011 he planned to strengthen state institutions and keep the state as provider of free health and education.

total-state.rationale: In 2011 he said the state should hand non-strategic activities to the non-state sector and decentralize powers.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He defended the state's role in running the economy and providing free health and education against privatization in 2021.

private-courts-defense.rationale: The constitution he oversaw keeps armed forces and the administration of justice in state institutions.

decide-locally.rationale: In 2011 he called for gradual decentralization of powers from central government to local administrations and state enterprises, within a unitary state.

leader-cult.rationale: In December 2016 he announced legislation so that Fidel's name and image would not name institutions, streets or monuments, in line with Fidel's wish.

rule-by-example.rationale: He demanded exemplary conduct from Party members but also insisted on strict legality and enforcement.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: In 2015 he told the UN that interventions in states' internal affairs on alleged human-rights grounds are unacceptable, and in 2011 he called NATO's Libya intervention brutal.

non-intervention.rationale: In 2015 he endorsed the CELAC commitment not to intervene directly or indirectly in any state's internal affairs, and repeated it in 2021.

national-self-determination.rationale: In 2015 he said every state has the inalienable right to choose its political, economic, social and cultural system, and backed independence for Puerto Rico.

force-without-un.rationale: He said Cuba rejects use of force, aggression and wars of conquest and demanded that disputes be settled peacefully under the UN Charter.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He said Cuba rejects aggression and wars of conquest, and the constitution defines armed forces' mission as defence of independence and sovereignty.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He rejected aggression and wars of conquest in 2011 and the constitution calls wars of aggression or conquest an international crime.

national-mission.rationale: He insisted every state may choose its own system and that no state may intervene in another's.

arms-reduction.rationale: In 2015 he said nuclear arsenals should be eliminated and criticised $1.7 trillion in annual military spending; the constitution calls for general disarmament.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He kept large armed forces and obligatory service, reaffirmed the doctrine of war of all the people in 2016 and 2021, and urged more military training.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He repeatedly demanded return of the Guantánamo base territory, calling its occupation illegal, and Cuba hosts no foreign bases.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: The constitution rejects the existence, proliferation and use of nuclear weapons, and in 2015 he said nuclear arsenals should be eliminated.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He condemned colonial domination, 'recolonization' and the plunder of peoples, and demanded reparations for colonialism and slavery.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He denounced colonial conquest and plunder as causes of underdevelopment and called Puerto Rico's colonial status unjust.

dominated-front.rationale: He built unity through CELAC and ALBA against US hegemony and deepened ties with China, Vietnam, Russia and Venezuela, rejecting NATO's expansion.

close-ties-china.rationale: In 2021 he reported excellent relations with China and relevant economic projects, while also restoring relations with the US.

nation-first.rationale: He stressed international cooperation, sending 65,000 Cuban personnel to 89 countries and calling for joint action on climate, health and poverty.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The constitution recognises solidarity with peoples fighting for liberation and he said Cuba once chose solidarity acts 'considered terrorist' when cornered, but he stated no policy for his own presidency.

party-own-road.rationale: He said Cuba would update its own model, citing China and Vietnam 'with differences', and in 2015 stressed each state's right to choose its system.

defeat-communism.rationale: As First Secretary of the Communist Party he declared socialism irrevocable and described efforts to restore capitalism as a threat to be fought.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He led the Communist Party and the 2011 'updating' to build a prosperous and sustainable socialism, rejecting a third path or restoration of capitalism.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2011 he said the lack of political will in industrialised nations prevents urgent action against devastating climate change, and in 2015 that it endangers the human species.

limit-growth.rationale: His programme aims at faster economic growth and development, with no cap for environmental reasons.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He located the causes of poverty in colonialism, imperialism and unequal distribution of wealth, not in population growth.

notes: Evidence is mainly his own speeches and party programmes plus the 2019 constitution, whose drafting commission he chaired; constitution-based answers are medium because they are a collective text. Secondhand reports (HRW, IPS, press) are used only for the treatment of dissidents, the 2008 death-sentence commutations and the 2013 migration reform, and are medium at most. Judgment calls: the 2011 term-limit proposal and his 2018 departure make term-limits high; repression answers rest on HRW and so stay medium; dynastic-succession, death-penalty, same-sex marriage and abortion were left null because his own position was not found (he succeeded his brother, not a child; the death penalty remains in the penal code but he commuted nearly all sentences in 2008). The 2013 migration reform and the 2008 commutations (reported by El Dínamo and IPS) were checked but matched no statement exactly..
